issues.body: `all(isinstance(row, dict) ...)` only validates each row's outer type. The matcher still evaluates `marker in (i.get("body") or "")`, which raises `TypeError` for a row such as `{"body": 42}`, and then reads `i["number"]`, which raises `KeyError` for `{"body": "<matching marker>"}` without `number` (the title fallback has the same indexed read). Thus a successful `gh` call returning malformed-but-object-shaped JSON can still propagate out of `main()` and take down upsert/recovery-close. The new tests exercise only scalar rows, so they do not detect this remaining boundary hole.
issues.fix_hint: Validate the complete row shape needed by the matcher before using any row (including a usable issue number and string-or-null `title`/`body`), refusing the whole listing on any invalid row, or rewrite matching so every JSON value is handled without exception while preserving whole-payload refusal. Add wrapped `run_main` cases for an object with non-string `body` and a matching object missing/invalid `number`, asserting warning, no payload echo, and no mutation.
issues.title: Malformed issue objects still escape the payload guard and crash the tick

verdict.summary: The added all-dicts check correctly prevents scalar rows from reaching `.get()`, and the new main-path assertions meaningfully verify soft-skip, payload redaction, and absence of mutations in both watchdog modes. However, the validation stops at the container type. A syntactically valid JSON object can still have a missing `number` or a non-string `body`; both reach the matcher and can raise, defeating the stated goal of degrading on an unusable successful `gh issue list` payload. The row schema must be validated (or matching made total) and tested before this is complete.
